decision_summary: LAPD let its three-year Flock Safety contract expire without renewal on July 11, 2026, cutting off access to 138 pole-mounted ALPR cameras. The move followed a July 2026 Inspector General audit that found 161 false hot-list alerts and recommended pausing deployments until enforceable data-privacy safeguards exist; the Police Commission voted July 14 to pause new camera installations.
notes: Contract start not pinned to an exact date (reporting says cameras operated since July 2023); left null. Multiple outlets report LAPD began renegotiating a new deal within days of expiry; status may need revisiting if a new contract is signed.

decision_summary: On January 13, 2026, the Santa Cruz City Council voted 6-1 to terminate the city's Flock Safety contract, making it the first California jurisdiction to do so. The termination followed the police chief's admission that camera data had been illegally shared with out-of-state agencies, including 190 searches run for ICE.
notes: Contract end ~2026-02-12 reflects the 30-day termination notice (contract had been scheduled to expire 2026-03-27). Camera count (8) and ~300k vehicles/month figure from secondary reporting; primary council record confirms the vote, not the count.

decision_summary: On February 24, 2026, the Mountain View City Council voted unanimously to terminate the city's Flock Safety ALPR pilot contract. Police Chief Mike Canfield had already shut off all 30 cameras on February 2 after a department audit found federal and out-of-state agencies had accessed city ALPR data for over a year without authorization.
notes: Primary source is the city's own news release. The unauthorized-access discovery (a 'national lookup' setting enabled without city knowledge) is what triggered the shutdown and is documented across all three sources.

decision_summary: Grass Valley PD cancelled its Flock Safety contract in August 2026 following a 60-day internal review that found hundreds of thousands of outside-agency queries against department data, and removed all cameras within days. In early September, at least two cameras were reinstalled without department permission after Flock's systems treated the takedown as equipment failure; the department removed them again.
notes: Cancellation letter dated 2026-08-11; public announcement 2026-08-12. Camera count not reported in any source; left null. The unauthorized reinstallation episode is corroborated by TechSpot, KCRA, and GVPD statements.

decision_summary: San Jose PD operates one of the largest Flock ALPR networks in California (516 cameras as of 2026), expanded from a 2021-2022 pilot under council authorizations that allow option terms through June 30, 2034. The program faces two lawsuits over warrantless database searches, and in 2026 the council tightened controls (30-day retention, installation limits) and directed staff to explore alternative vendors.
notes: Camera count grew 474 (2025) to 516 (Sept 2026); using the latest figure. Contract structure is option-based rather than a single fixed term, so contract_end is null; the nine one-year options run through 2034-06-30 per 2023 council action. A SJPD officer was fired in 2026 for abusing ALPR database access.

decision_summary: On February 22, 2024, the Fresno City Council approved an updated three-year Flock Safety agreement not to exceed $1,498,690.41 covering ALPR cameras and software; the department reports 70 cameras deployed. The contract is set to expire later in 2026 and a renewal vote is expected, with community groups already petitioning against renewal.
notes: Annual cost is derived ($1,498,690.41 / 3 years), not a billed figure. Contract start is ambiguous across sources (2023 per local TV, 2024 per council action); left null. Flock order form on file with the city confirms a 36-month initial term and 30-day retention.

decision_summary: On February 3, 2026, the Woodland City Council unanimously approved a two-year Flock Safety contract extension not to exceed $300,000, covering 36-38 ALPR cameras. The department publishes ALPR usage data on a city transparency page and conducts monthly audits of Flock database searches.
notes: Annual cost derived ($300,000 / 2 years); ~$160,000 of the total is reimbursed by local cannabis dispensaries per the staff report, so the city's net cost is lower. Contract end 2028-02-03 assumes a full two-year term from approval; not explicitly stated.

decision_summary: On March 31, 2026, the Stockton City Council voted 7-0 to approve a $3.15 million Flock amendment adding six 'Drone as First Responder' drones, bringing the total Flock contract to about $5.4 million through April 14, 2031. The department operates 120 Flock ALPR cameras; residents urged the council in August 2026 to terminate the contract over privacy and data-sharing concerns.
notes: Annual cost left null because the $5.4M bundles cameras, drones, and software over varying terms. Vice Mayor Jason Lee floated a special public-safety meeting on Flock in Sept 2026; no date set. Camera count (120) stated at the March meeting.

decision_summary: Oxnard PD suspended use of all 19 fixed Flock cameras in February 2026 after a 2025 audit revealed unauthorized nationwide database access to the department's ALPR data despite 'California only' settings. Police Chief Jason Benites said the suspension remains until the department is fully confident data is secure; the department planned to revisit a fixed-platform ALPR system later.
notes: Suspended, not terminated: no council termination vote found as of 2026-09-25, so status is pending rather than cancelled. Exact suspension date not pinned (February 2026 per multiple outlets); a city news release dated 2026-02-27 exists but was not directly retrievable.

decision_summary: On March 24, 2026, the Berkeley City Council delayed a vote on a roughly $2 million Flock Safety expansion (cameras, investigative software, drones) after hundreds of residents spoke against it past 1:30 a.m.; the item was continued to June 2. The city's existing 52-ALPR Flock network remains active under an interim extension while the city runs a competitive RFP for surveillance technology.
notes: Mayor Adena Ishii reversed course to oppose any Flock renewal; the Police Accountability Board recommended against the contract. The interim-extension-during-RFP detail comes from meeting summaries; the June 2 outcome was not confirmed as of 2026-09-25.
